title: PhaseGate traffic carveout engine: policy config for staged rollouts, shadowing, and auto-rollback
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a policy-driven "PhaseGate" traffic carving engine to support staged canary rollouts, directional shadowing, and automatic rollback. The engine should express ramp schedules (time and request-volume based), safety gates (SLO thresholds, statistical significance windows), and emergency kill-switch hooks. Deliverables: a config DSL for rollout policies, runtime validator, integration points for console and SDK, simulation harness for batching and latency-sensitive workloads, and a rollout audit trail for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Config DSL that encodes: step percentages, step durations, minimum sample size, metric guards (p95 latency, error-rate), and shadow-only routes
Runtime enforcer that can apply traffic splits and shadow copies without request duplication >1% overhead on p50 latency in staging
Auto-rollback policy that triggers when configured guardrails breach for 2 consecutive evaluation windows
Console UI hooks and rollout API documented with examples for A/B, canary, and shadowing modes
Simulation harness that reproduces a high-throughput workload (10k rps) and outputs per-step expected token cost and 95% CI for metric deltas
comments: 2026-02-20 - Ava Martinez: Created RFC draft and initial config examples. Linked behavior matrix and proposed DSL (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/PhaseGate+Rollout+RFC).

2026-02-27 - Liam O'Connor: Spike complete on runtime hooks. Verified ability to programmatically create shadow routes in staging without touching production routing layer. Notes: shadowing adds ~0.7% p50 overhead in infra-optimized path.
2026-03-03 - Design review (Sofia Patel): Requesting explicit UI affordances for emergency rollback, and human-readable step descriptions. Added label 'safety-guards' to ticket.
2026-03-06 - Engineering: Implemented initial validator that rejects ambiguous step schedules (e.g., overlapping time windows). Unit tests added: 42 passing, 1 flaky guard test marked xfail.

2026-03-10 - PM feedback (Rajiv Khanna): Ensure canary policies support both absolute token-count and percentage-of-traffic gating. Added dependency on cost-metering (ENG-41208) for accurate per-step cost estimates.
2026-03-12 - Security review kickoff: confirmed audit trail schema with Security. Logging must include model version, step id, gradient of traffic, and kill-switch actor (console/service).

2026-03-14 - Simulation results attached: baseline vs canary with KV cache hit variance. Key finding: short 30s evaluation windows undercount transient p95 spikes; recommend default 3-minute windows for production rollouts. Simulation dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/sim/phasegate-90345

Follow-ups: schedule integration with rollout telemetry pipeline, finalize DSL error messages, and add a throttled graceful-fail mode (route to fallback model) if rollout controller becomes overloaded.
notes: Trade-offs considered: tight evaluation windows reduce time-to-detect regressions but increase false positives; we bias toward slightly longer windows for models with high latency variance.
Implementation decision: use a two-stage gating check (fast-check on p50/p90, deep-check on p95/error-rate with statistical significance).
Rollback semantics: soft-rollback (pause and hold traffic at previous step) vs hard-rollback (revert to previous model). Default = soft-rollback + pager alert; allow admin override.
Operational playbook: when guardrail fires, automated snapshot of request traces for 2 minutes is stored in cold storage and a short summary posted to incident channel.
